Name: CIS Controls v8.0 for AWS
Description: The CIS Amazon Web Services Foundations Benchmark provides prescriptive guidance for configuring security options for a subset of Amazon Web Services with an emphasis on foundational, testable, and architecture agnostic settings.

Requirements.Description: Inventory and Control of Enterprise Assets

Checks.name: Ensure EC2 AMIs Are Not Publicly Shared
Checks.description: Evaluates Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) to verify that launch permissions are not configured as public, helping prevent unauthorized access to internal disk images.

Checks.name: Ensure EBS Snapshots Are Not Publicly Shared
Checks.description: Evaluates EBS snapshot sharing permissions to identify snapshots that are publicly accessible and could expose copied volume data.

Checks.name: Prevent Public Access to ECR Repositories
Checks.description: Checks ECR repository permissions to identify repositories that allow public access to container images.

Checks.name: Prevent Public Access to Amazon Redshift Clusters
Checks.description: Evaluates the Amazon Redshift cluster against the benchmark objective “Ensure Redshift clusters do not have a public endpoint.” It helps identify configuration gaps that could weaken security configuration, exposure reduction, and control assurance.

Checks.name: Prevent Public Access to OpenSearch Domains
Checks.description: Evaluates Amazon OpenSearch domain network and access configuration to identify domains exposed publicly when access should be restricted.

Attributes.Section: CSC 1 – Inventory and Control of Enterprise Assets
Attributes.Description: Use Prowler to identify exposed or misconfigured cloud resources as part of maintaining an accurate and controlled asset inventory.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Exposed resources and public snapshots indicate weak control over the asset surface and inventory governance.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Uncontrolled or publicly exposed assets increase the risk of data breach and unauthorized access.
Attributes.RemediationProcedure: Perform the following to establish security contact information: **From Console:** 1. Click on your account name at the top right corner of the console. 2. From the drop-down menu Click `My Account`  3. Scroll down to the `Alternate Contacts` section 4. Enter contact information in the `Security` section **From Command Line:** Run the following command with the following input parameters: --email-address, --name, and --phone-number. ``` aws account put-alternate-contact --alternate-contact-type SECURITY  ```  **Note:** Consider specifying an internal email distribution list to ensure emails are regularly monitored by more than one individual.
Attributes.AuditProcedure: Perform the following to determine if security contact information is present: **From Console:** 1. Click on your account name at the top right corner of the console 2. From the drop-down menu Click `My Account`  3. Scroll down to the `Alternate Contacts` section 4. Ensure contact information is specified in the `Security` section **From Command Line:** 1. Run the following command: ```  aws account get-alternate-contact --alternate-contact-type SECURITY ``` 2. Ensure proper contact information is specified for the `Security` contact.

Requirements.Description: Inventory and Control of Software Assets

Checks.name: Attach AWS Lambda Functions to a VPC Where Required
Checks.description: Checks whether AWS Lambda functions are attached to a VPC when required by the benchmark's workload-isolation control.

Checks.name: Prevent Public Access to EKS Cluster Endpoints
Checks.description: Checks EKS cluster endpoint access settings to identify public exposure that is not intended by the deployment's access model.

Checks.name: Prevent Plaintext Secrets in ECS Task Definitions
Checks.description: Checks ECS task definitions for secrets supplied as plaintext configuration rather than being retrieved from an approved secrets-management service.

Attributes.Section: CSC 2 – Inventory and Control of Software Assets
Attributes.Description: Map Prowler checks around managed runtimes and workloads to software inventory and control requirements.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Knowing which workloads are exposed and how they are configured is key to managing software risk.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Untracked or misconfigured workloads can bypass patching, monitoring and data protection controls.

Checks.name: Prevent Unintended Public Access to S3 Buckets
Checks.description: Evaluates S3 access configuration to identify buckets with unintended public access paths.

Checks.name: Prevent Public Write Access Through S3 Bucket Policies
Checks.description: Evaluates S3 bucket policies for public write permissions that could allow untrusted principals to modify or inject data.

Checks.name: Block Public Access to S3 Buckets
Checks.description: Checks whether S3 bucket public access is effectively blocked by the applicable public-access settings.

Checks.name: Enable Server-Side Encryption for S3 Buckets
Checks.description: Checks whether S3 objects are protected by server-side encryption at rest.

Checks.name: Enable KMS Key Rotation
Checks.description: Checks AWS KMS key-rotation configuration to identify keys for which rotation is not enabled where applicable.

Checks.name: Encrypt Amazon RDS Clusters at Rest
Checks.description: Checks whether Amazon RDS cluster storage is encrypted at rest to protect database data and underlying storage.

Checks.name: Enable EBS Encryption by Default
Checks.description: Checks whether EBS encryption by default is enabled in the relevant Region, reducing the chance that newly created EBS volumes are left unencrypted.

Checks.name: Prevent Public Access to Amazon SNS Topics
Checks.description: Evaluates the Amazon SNS topic against the benchmark objective “Ensure SNS topics do not allow global send or subscribe.” It helps identify configuration gaps that could weaken security configuration, exposure reduction, and control assurance.

Checks.name: Prevent Public Access to Amazon SQS Queues
Checks.description: Evaluates Amazon SQS queue resource policies to identify queues that can be accessed by unintended public principals.

Attributes.Description: Use Prowler checks to ensure encryption at rest, control of public access and secure key management.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: CIS Controls v8 requires strong safeguards around sensitive data in storage and in transit.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Improperly protected or publicly accessible data stores can lead directly to regulatory impact and breach disclosure.

Requirements.Description: Secure Configuration of Enterprise Assets and Software

Checks.name: Enable AWS Config Recording Across Regions
Checks.description: Evaluates the AWS Config configuration recorder against the benchmark objective “Ensure AWS Config is enabled in all regions.” It helps identify configuration gaps that could weaken configuration visibility and drift detection.

Checks.name: Enable the AWS Config Recorder
Checks.description: Checks whether AWS Config recording is enabled so supported resource configuration changes can be inventoried and assessed.

Checks.name: Enable AWS Security Hub

Requirements.Description: Account Management (Access Control Management in some summaries)

Checks.name: Require MFA for Administrative IAM Access
Checks.description: Checks whether IAM principals with administrative access are required to use multi-factor authentication, adding protection to highly privileged access.

Checks.name: Prevent Customer-Managed Administrative Policies from Being Attached
Checks.description: Checks customer-managed IAM policy permissions for full (*:*) administrative privileges and identifies overly broad permissions that can give principals unrestricted control over AWS resources.

Checks.name: Identify IAM Policies That Allow Privilege Escalation
Checks.description: Evaluates IAM policy permissions for combinations that could enable a principal to elevate privileges beyond its intended authorization.

Checks.name: Restrict Overly Permissive Custom Role-Assumption Policies
Checks.description: Evaluates customer-managed IAM policies for overly permissive role-assumption permissions that could enable unintended cross-role or cross-account access.

Attributes.Description: Prowler IAM policy and admin privilege checks reflect CIS v8 requirements for tightly managed accounts and roles.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: Excessive privileges and poor policy hygiene are high-value attack paths.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Privilege escalation or over-permissive policies can allow full compromise from a single account.

Checks.name: Require MFA for the AWS Root User
Checks.description: Checks whether MFA protects the AWS root identity, adding a second authentication factor to the account's most privileged identity.

Checks.name: Ensure the AWS Root User Has No Access Keys
Checks.description: Checks whether the AWS root identity has active programmatic access keys, which can provide highly privileged access outside normal role-based controls.

Checks.name: Avoid Using the AWS Root User for Routine Tasks
Checks.description: Evaluates the AWS account root identity and IAM account settings against the benchmark objective “Avoid the use of the 'root' account.” It helps identify configuration gaps that could weaken identity security and least-privilege enforcement.

Checks.name: Require MFA for IAM Users with Console Access
Checks.description: Checks whether IAM users who can sign in to the console are protected by multi-factor authentication.

Checks.name: Enforce an AWS IAM Account Password Policy
Checks.description: Evaluates the AWS account's IAM password policy settings to identify missing or weak requirements for password length, complexity, reuse, or expiration.

Checks.name: Require Uppercase Characters in IAM Passwords
Checks.description: Checks whether the IAM password policy requires at least one uppercase character in each password.

Checks.name: Require Lowercase Characters in IAM Passwords
Checks.description: Checks whether the IAM password policy requires at least one lowercase character in each password.

Checks.name: Require Symbols in IAM Passwords
Checks.description: Checks whether the IAM password policy requires at least one symbol in each password.

Checks.name: Require Numbers in IAM Passwords
Checks.description: Checks whether the IAM password policy requires at least one numeric character in each password.

Checks.name: Rotate IAM Access Keys Within 90 Days
Checks.description: Evaluates the IAM user against the benchmark objective “Ensure access keys are rotated every 90 days or less.” It helps identify configuration gaps that could weaken identity security and least-privilege enforcement.

Checks.name: Disable or Remove Unused IAM Access Keys
Checks.description: Checks IAM access-key activity to identify keys that have not been used within the applicable period and should be disabled or removed after validation.

Attributes.Description: Use Prowler IAM checks to cover MFA, password policy strength, key rotation and unused credentials.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: CIS v8 emphasises strong authentication, controlled identity lifecycle and secret management.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Weak identity controls directly increase account takeover and unauthorized access risk.

Checks.name: Prevent Security Groups from Allowing Any Port from the Internet
Checks.description: Evaluates EC2 security-group inbound rules for unrestricted internet access to arbitrary ports, which can expose services that were intended to be reachable only from trusted networks.

Checks.name: Restrict Internet Ingress to SSH on Port 22
Checks.description: Checks whether EC2 security groups permit SSH (TCP port 22) from the public internet; restrict this access to approved administration sources.

Checks.name: Restrict Internet Ingress to RDP on Port 3389
Checks.description: Checks whether EC2 security groups permit Remote Desktop Protocol (TCP port 3389) from the public internet, reducing the risk of direct remote-administration exposure.

Checks.name: Restrict Security Group Ingress to Trusted Sources
Checks.description: Evaluates EC2 security-group ingress rules to verify that inbound traffic is limited to required ports and trusted source ranges.

Checks.name: Enable VPC Flow Logs
Checks.description: Checks whether VPC Flow Logs are enabled to capture network traffic metadata for investigation and monitoring.

Attributes.Description: Use security-group and VPC-related checks to map to CIS v8 network hardening requirements.
Attributes.RationaleStatement: CIS v8 expects controlled remote administration and restricted ingress/egress on networks.
Attributes.ImpactStatement: Overly permissive security groups and missing flow logs increase lateral movement and exfiltration risk.
